facts.text: While devotees see divine intervention in the flag's motion, meteorologists and aerodynamicists explain that high-altitude oceanic boundary currents, local thermal eddies off the temple's curved superstructure, and coastal sea-breeze reversals create local air drafts that move contrary to ground-level wind perceptions.

facts.text: Architectural analysts indicate the temple does cast shadows, but its tapering curvilinear profile, orientation to cardinal directions, and wide elevated podium cause the shadow to fall primarily onto its own recesses and adjoining roof surfaces rather than stretching across the surrounding ground.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The Nila Chakra is made of ashtadhatu and measures 3.5 metres in height with an outer circumference facing all cardinal coordinates.
facts.text: The Neela Chakra positioned atop the shikhara is an octagonal alloy disc measuring approximately 3.5 metres in diameter.

facts.text: Culinary observers and thermal engineers debate the cooking phenomenon, with practitioners maintaining the top pot finishes first, while physicists attribute rapid heating to steam convection and narrow vertical drafts created by the porous clay vessel assembly.

facts.text: The Skanda Purana declares that the holy site of Purushottama Kshetra constitutes the eternal physical form of the Supreme Being on the eastern shore of India.

facts.text: In 1975, the Archaeological Survey of India officially brought the 12th-century Jagannath Temple under national statutory preservation via notification S.O. 560.
